name: A forward and a scaled leg
brief:
The payoff library has an abstract `Payoff`, whose pure virtual `operator()(double spot) const` gives the payoff at a spot, and a `Call`; both are loaded. Write two more classes derived from `Payoff`. `Forward(k)` pays `spot - k`, which is negative below the strike. `Scaled(qty, inner)` owns another payoff through a `std::unique_ptr<Payoff>` and pays `qty` times it; a negative `qty` is a short position.

Short two forwards struck at 100: at a spot of 90 each forward pays -10, so a `Scaled` with `qty` -2 around a `Forward(100.0)` pays 20.
constraints: `qty` may be any finite number, including 0 and negative values.
A `Scaled` may hold another `Scaled`, and the tests call it through a `const Payoff&`.
hint: `Scaled` keeps the `unique_ptr` it is given with `std::move`, and calls `(*inner_)(spot)`, which dispatches to the real type.

examples.note: Short two forwards at a spot below the strike gains.
A scaled leg inside a scaled leg: 3 times -0.5 times 20.

tests.call: []{ Scaled s(2.0, std::make_unique<Forward>(10.0)); const Payoff& p = s; return p(15.0); }()

[]{ std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Payoff>> book; book.push_back(std::make_unique<Scaled>(-2.0, std::make_unique<Call>(110.0))); book.push_back(std::make_unique<Forward>(95.0)); double v = 0; for (const auto& p : book) v += (*p)(120.0); return v; }()

how: Submit runs 11 hidden tests. Each answer must be within a relative 1e-9 of the expected value.
notes: `Scaled` holds a `Payoff` it does not know the type of, so the call through `*inner_` must be virtual.
Owning the inner leg by `std::unique_ptr` means the `Scaled` frees it, and a book of legs frees everything.
A forward has no floor at 0; that floor is what makes a call a call.

planted.slip: The forward is floored at 0, which makes it a call.
Drops the sign of qty, so a short position counts as long.
The forward pays strike less spot, the wrong way round.
The strike is stored as a float, so a strike such as 99.9 is slightly off.
